Lemma hypergraph_snake_left (X : C) : to (@unit_left C _ X) ∘ bimap (hcc_counit X (F := scfa X)) id[X] ∘ from (@tensor_assoc C _ X X X) ∘ bimap id[X] (hcc_unit X (F := scfa X)) ∘ from (@unit_right C _ X) ≈ id[X].   (with hypergraph_snake_right at :273, the mirror identity) — the two snake/yanking equations of the theorem, proved rather than assumed, from the Frobenius law plus the monoid-unit and comonoid-counit laws.

statement_record.book: Theorem 5.87: the prop Rel_R of R-relations is a compact closed category in which every object n ∈ ℕ is dual to itself, n = n*. The witnesses are supplied by the preceding prose: the cup and cap signal flow graphs of Eq. (5.86), with behaviors {(0,(x,x)) : x ∈ R} ⊆ R^0 × R^2 and {((x,x),0) : x ∈ R} ⊆ R^2 × R^0, serve as η_1 and ε_1 at the object 1, monoidal products give the duality data at every n, and the snake equations are the graphically checked claim that three displayed signal flow graphs denote the same relation. Notably this holds for Rel_R but NOT for Mat(R), since cup and cap are not graphs of linear maps.
statement_record.intree: `Class CompactClosed` (Structure/Monoidal/CompactClosed.v:139) over a `SymmetricMonoidal` base, with fields `dual : C -> C`, `cc_unit X : I ~> dual X ⨂ X`, `cc_counit X : X ⨂ dual X ~> I` and the two snake identities, matching the chapter-4 definition. `Hypergraph_CompactClosed` proves the abstract form of the theorem: for any hypergraph category, `dual X := X` — every object is its own dual — with cup δ ∘ η and cap ε ∘ μ built from the special commutative Frobenius algebra on each object, and both snake laws discharged (`hypergraph_snake_left`, `hypergraph_snake_right`). `Cospan_Hypergraph` supplies a concrete hypergraph category, so the self-dual compact-closed structure has an in-tree witness (over FinSet).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker only in its instantiation, not in its content: the general theorem 'every hypergraph category is compact closed with every object self-dual, snake laws proved' is in-tree at full strength and is inhabited, but it is never applied to Rel_R, which does not exist. The gap is one of models, not of the statement. Note also a genuine hypothesis difference: the in-tree route DERIVES self-duality from a special commutative Frobenius structure on every object (the `Hypergraph` class), whereas the book exhibits η and ε directly for Rel_R and checks the snakes graphically; there is no in-tree derivation of `CompactClosed` from bare cup/cap data supplied by hand, so a future Rel_R would have to be routed through `Hypergraph` or instantiate `Class CompactClosed` from scratch.
